key_insight: Representing distinct lighting factors as explicit attribute tokens enables precise, continuous control over multiple illumination attributes in image relighting, yielding disentangled and editable lighting changes.
problem_solved: Provides a practical way to manipulate complex, interdependent lighting attributes (intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, 3D light position) in photographs, addressing limited control and entanglement in prior relighting methods while leveraging synthetic annotations with real-image augmentation.
method: Formulate relighting as a conditional image-generation task where attribute tokens parameterize individual illumination factors (intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, 3D positions).
Encode desired lighting attributes as tokens fed to a generative model to produce relit images with continuous, disentangled control.
Train primarily on a large synthetic dataset with ground-truth lighting annotations and supplement with a small set of real images to improve real-world generalization.
impact: Enables fine-grained, user-controllable relighting for applications like photo editing, AR/VR content creation, and data augmentation; simplifies integration of lighting edits into generative pipelines for practitioners.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing image input, attribute tokens, and generator producing relit output.
Before/after image grid with interactive sliders illustrating continuous control over intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, and light position.
Token-to-attribute mapping: icons for each lighting attribute (bulb/intensity, color swatch, ambient glow, surface diffuse, 3D position) linked to token vectors.
Comparison chart (qualitative examples and brief quantitative summary) vs prior relighting methods to highlight improved controllability.
paper_title: TokenLight: Precise Lighting Control in Images using Attribute Tokens
paper_authors: Sumit Chaturvedi, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Mengwei Ren, Jingyuan Liu, He Zhang
